recipe: 1. Pressure cook soaked kala chana with a pinch of salt for 4-5 whistles until tender. 2. Drain excess water and transfer to a mixing bowl. 3. Add chopped onions, tomatoes, cucumber, cumin powder, black salt, and lemon juice. 4. Toss well and garnish with fresh coriander.
benefits: High in dietary iron, folate, and insoluble dietary fiber. Helps prevent anemia, manages insulin sensitivity, and sustains energy for hours.
tips: Save the boiled chana water (aquafaba) to add to your dal or soup for extra mineral fortification.

name: Dalma (Odia Lentil & Root Veg Stew) with Steamed Brown Rice
ingredients: Toor Dal & Moong Dal mix - 50g raw
Panch Phoron (Five spice mix) & Dry red chili - 1/2 tsp
recipe: 1. Pressure cook dal and chunky cut vegetables with turmeric, ginger, and salt until tender. 2. Temper ghee with panch phoron and dry chili, pour over the simmering dalma. 3. Sprinkle aromatic roasted cumin-chili powder (bhaja masala) on top. 4. Serve with hot steamed brown rice.
benefits: Traditional Odia temple cuisine that combines healing lentils with gut-soothing raw papaya enzymes (papain) and antioxidant-rich pumpkin.
tips: Raw papaya in Dalma aids natural protein digestion and keeps the stomach light.

name: Curd Rice with Pomegranate & Mustard Tempering (Gut Healing Bowl)
ingredients: Cooked Rice (slightly overcooked & mashed) - 60g raw (180g cooked)
Mustard seeds, Curry leaves, Ginger & Hing - 1/2 tsp oil tempering
recipe: 1. Mash warm cooked rice gently and let it cool to room temperature. 2. Fold in fresh creamy curd, salt, grated cucumber, and pomegranate pearls. 3. Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, minced ginger, and a pinch of hing in 1/2 tsp oil. 4. Pour the sizzling tadka over the curd rice and mix gently.
benefits: Ultimate gut-restorative meal. Supplies millions of live Lactobacillus cultures to rebalance intestinal flora and soothe gut inflammation.
tips: Always mix curd when rice has cooled down to room temperature so live probiotic cultures remain intact.

name: Chicken Keema Matar with 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas (Lean Minced)
ingredients: Garam Masala, Kasuri Methi, Coriander, Lemon
recipe: 1. Heat 1 tsp oil, sauté onions, ginger-garlic, and tomatoes until soft. 2. Add minced chicken keema, green peas, turmeric, chili powder, and garam masala; sauté on high heat for 5 minutes. 3. Add 1/2 cup water, cover, and cook for 8 minutes until juicy and thick. 4. Serve with 2 hot phulkas and lemon wedges.
benefits: Packed with 38g high-quality animal protein, dietary iron, and zinc with low saturated fat content.
tips: Using minced breast meat instead of dark meat cuts the total fat content by over 60%.

name: Tandoori Fish Tikka & Brown Rice Platter (Surmai / Basa)
servingUnit: 1 Platter (150g Fish Tikka + Brown Rice + Dip)
ingredients: Hung Curd Tandoori Marinade with Ajwain & Lemon - 2 tbsp
Mint Yogurt Chutney & Sliced Onions - 1 bowl
recipe: 1. Marinate fish cubes in hung curd, ajwain (carom seeds), tandoori masala, and lemon for 15 minutes. 2. Pan grill or bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until flaky and charred at edges. 3. Serve hot fish tikka with steamed brown rice, mint chutney, and lemon slices.
benefits: High protein, ultra-lean, and loaded with heart-healthy omega-3s and carom seeds for rapid digestion.
tips: Ajwain in the fish marinade eliminates any fishy odor and aids rapid protein assimilation.

name: Jain Green Moong Dal Khichdi with Besan Kadhi (No Onion, No Garlic)
ingredients: Low-fat Curd & Besan (for Kadhi) - 100g curd + 1 tbsp besan
Cumin seeds, Mustard seeds, Curry leaves, Hing, Turmeric
recipe: 1. Pressure cook split moong dal and rice with turmeric, salt, and water for 4 whistles until soft and creamy. 2. Whisk curd with besan, water, turmeric, and simmer into a light kadhi; temper with cumin, curry leaves, and hing in ghee. 3. Serve comforting hot khichdi paired with warm kadhi.
benefits: 100% Sattvic / Jain compliant with zero root vegetables, onions, or garlic. Extremely soothing for gastrointestinal recovery.
tips: A pinch of hing (asafoetida) in the tempering provides natural digestive enzyme stimulation.

name: Ragi Dosa with Vegetable Sambar & Tomato Chutney (2 Dosas)
ingredients: Urad Dal & Rice Flour - 1 tbsp each
recipe: 1. Mix ragi flour with a little rice flour, salt, and water to make a thin lacy batter. 2. Pour over a hot tawa from outside to inside like rava dosa. 3. Drizzle drops of oil and cook until crisp. 4. Serve hot with vegetable sambar and tangy tomato chutney.
benefits: Rich in calcium (344mg/100g), polyphenols, and slow-burning dietary fiber. Strengthens bone density and stabilizes insulin.
tips: No fermentation needed! Batter can be whisked together in 2 minutes for an instant nutritious breakfast.

name: Sprouted Moong & Pomegranate Protein Chaat (No-Cook Bowl)
ingredients: Chaat Masala, Roasted Cumin, Lemon Juice - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. In a mixing bowl, combine sprouted moong, diced cucumber, tomatoes, and ruby pomegranate pearls. 2. Sprinkle chaat masala, roasted cumin, black salt, and freshly squeezed lemon juice. 3. Toss lightly and enjoy fresh and crunchy.
benefits: Zero cooking required! Packed with living digestive enzymes, bioavailable Vitamin C, and clean alkaline plant protein.
tips: Steam the sprouts for 60 seconds if you have sensitive digestion or IBS.

name: Kashmiri Nadru Yakhni (Lotus Stem Yogurt Curry) with Brown Rice
ingredients: Fennel powder (Saunf), Dry Ginger (Sonth), Whole spices - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Slice and boil lotus stem with salt until tender. 2. Whisk curd with dry ginger, fennel powder, and cloves; simmer on low heat while stirring continuously to prevent curdling. 3. Add boiled lotus stem slices and let simmer for 10 minutes. 4. Serve aromatic mild yakhni with steamed brown rice.
benefits: Lotus root is rich in dietary fiber, potassium, and Vitamin C, promoting blood pressure regulation and respiratory health.
tips: Keep stirring the yogurt gravy continuously until the first boil to maintain a velvety smooth texture.

name: Odia Chana Dal & Coconut (Chholar Dal) with 2 Multigrain Rotis
ingredients: Ginger, Cumin, Bay leaf, Cinnamon, Asafoetida (Hing) - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Pressure cook chana dal with turmeric, bay leaf, and ginger until cooked but holding its shape. 2. In 1 tsp ghee, fry tiny coconut slices until golden; add cumin, cinnamon, and hing. 3. Pour tempering over dal, simmer for 5 minutes until rich and thick. 4. Serve with 2 soft multigrain rotis and green salad.
benefits: Rich in zinc, protein, and dietary copper with low glycemic impact. Fresh coconut provides medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs) for steady energy.
tips: Do not mash chana dal; the individual intact grains provide a pleasant nutty bite.

name: Kerala Style Egg Roast with 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas
servingUnit: 2 Boiled Eggs in Roast Gravy + 2 Phulkas
ingredients: Curry leaves, Black Pepper, Fennel powder, Garam Masala - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Sauté sliced onions in coconut oil with curry leaves and ginger-garlic paste until caramelized dark golden brown. 2. Add tomatoes, black pepper, fennel powder, and turmeric. 3. Add halved hard boiled eggs and coat in the thick spicy masala for 4 minutes. 4. Serve hot with whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: Rich in high-bioavailability protein, lutein, and healthy lauric acid from coconut oil. Boosts immune function and satiety.
tips: Caramelizing the onions slowly on low heat creates the signature rich natural sweetness of authentic Kerala egg roast.

name: Goan Fish Curry with Steamed Rice & Kandi Podi Salad
servingUnit: 1 Bowl Goan Fish Curry + 1 Bowl Steamed Rice
ingredients: Kashmiri Chili, Coriander seeds, Kokum / Tamarind paste - 1 tbsp
recipe: 1. Grind roasted chilies, coriander seeds, garlic, and kokum into a smooth Goan masala paste. 2. Sauté paste in 1 tsp coconut oil, add light coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. 3. Add fish cubes and cook covered on medium-low for 6 minutes until tender. 4. Serve with steamed rice and cucumber salad.
benefits: Kokum is a natural antioxidant containing hydroxycitric acid (HCA), known for boosting metabolism, paired with clean ocean protein.
tips: Kokum gives the traditional authentic tang without the heavy acidity of artificial vinegars.

name: Soya Keema Matar Sandwich (High-Protein Quick Toast - 20g Protein)
ingredients: Soya Granules (Crushed Soya) - 40g dry (yields 100g cooked keema)
Pav Bhaji Masala & Lemon Juice - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Boil soya granules for 3 minutes, drain and squeeze dry. 2. Sauté with onions, peas, pav bhaji masala, and salt for 4 minutes. 3. Spread mint chutney on bread, fill with spicy soya keema, and toast on tawa/sandwich maker until golden and crispy.
benefits: High-protein snack alternative to processed paneer or cheese sandwiches, delivering 22g protein for only ₹20.
tips: Use soya granules rather than large chunks for an instant 3-minute cook time and perfect sandwich texture.

name: Paneer & Sprouts Stuffed Whole Wheat Kathi Roll
ingredients: Mint Yogurt Chutney & Chaat Masala - 2 tbsp
recipe: 1. Sauté paneer, sprouts, onions, and capsicum with chaat masala on high heat for 3 minutes. 2. Warm 2 whole wheat rotis, spread mint yogurt sauce, fill with spicy paneer-sprout mixture, roll tightly, and wrap in paper.
benefits: Portable complete meal for busy office workers and students. High in protein, crunch, and micronutrients.
tips: A drop of lemon juice and pickled onion strips inside the roll creates authentic Kolkata kathi roll flavor.

name: Overnight Mango Chia & Sattu Pudding Jar (Summer Superfood)
recipe: 1. In a jar, whisk sattu, chia seeds, cardamom, and milk together until smooth. 2. Layer with fresh sweet mango cubes. 3. Refrigerate overnight (or 2 hours) until chia forms a rich pudding. 4. Garnish with crushed pistachios and serve chilled.
benefits: Rich in soluble mucilage fiber, ALA Omega-3s, natural mango beta-carotene, and 12g sustained-release plant protein.
tips: Prep 3 jars on Sunday night for instant grabbed breakfasts through the busy work week.

name: Moong Dal Khichuri & Begun Bhaja (Bengali Comfort Thali)
ingredients: Eggplant Slices (Begun Bhaja) - 80g (pan roasted with turmeric)
Ginger, Green chili, Cumin, Bay leaf, Ghee - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Dry roast yellow moong dal until fragrant and golden. 2. Pressure cook roasted dal and rice with ginger, turmeric, bay leaf, peas, and tomatoes for 3 whistles. 3. Pan-sear eggplant slices dusted in turmeric and salt in 1/2 tsp oil. 4. Serve the hot comforting khichuri with begun bhaja.
benefits: Deeply comforting, restorative for the liver and gut, and forms a balanced vegetarian protein with high bioavailability.
tips: Roasting the moong dal before boiling gives the khichuri its iconic nutty Bengali aroma.

name: Jain Moong Dal Khichdi with Dahi & Ghee
recipe: 1. Wash moong dal and rice. Pressure cook with turmeric, salt, and water for 3 whistles. 2. Temper desi ghee with cumin, hing, and green chili. Pour over hot khichdi. 3. Serve hot with fresh curd.
benefits: Ultra easy on the digestive system, sattvic, high bioavailability protein.
tips: Add a pinch of roasted cumin powder over the curd.

name: Jain Paneer Makhani with 2 Phulkas & Salad
servingUnit: 1 bowl Jain Paneer Makhani + 2 whole wheat Phulkas + Cucumber slices
recipe: 1. Saute tomato puree in ghee with kasuri methi and spices. 2. Add cashew paste and water to form a silky gravy without onion or garlic. 3. Add cubed paneer and simmer 3 mins. 4. Serve with 2 fresh puffed phulkas.
benefits: Rich in calcium, casein protein, and sustained energy.
tips: Avoid ginger or garlic powders to adhere strictly to Jain guidelines.

name: Jain Lauki (Dudhi) Thepla with Fresh Curd (3 pieces)
servingUnit: 3 medium Lauki Theplas + 1 cup fresh Curd
recipe: 1. Grate fresh lauki (dudhi). Knead with atta, besan, curd, spices, and sesame seeds into a soft dough without adding extra water. 2. Roll thin theplas and roast with minimal oil on a hot tawa. 3. Serve with curd.
benefits: Hydrating, rich in dietary fiber, low glycemic index.
tips: Grating lauki fresh keeps the dough naturally moist.

name: Jain Raw Banana (Kela) Sabzi with 2 Phulkas & Moong Dal
servingUnit: 1 bowl Raw Banana Sabzi + 1 bowl Moong Dal + 2 Phulkas
ingredients: Mustard seeds, Hing, Turmeric, Coriander powder
recipe: 1. Peel and cube raw green banana. Steam until tender. 2. Temper oil with mustard seeds, hing, turmeric, and dry coriander. Toss raw banana cubes for 4 mins. 3. Serve with boiled moong dal and 2 phulkas.
benefits: Resistant starch for gut microbiome, completely root-free Jain staple.
tips: Raw banana absorbs spices well and offers the hearty texture of potatoes.

name: Jain Moong Dal Chilla with Tomato-Coriander Chutney (2 pieces)
recipe: 1. Grind soaked yellow moong dal with green chili, hing, and salt into a smooth batter. 2. Spread ladleful on hot non-stick tawa, drizzle drops of oil, and cook both sides until golden crisp. 3. Serve with fresh tomato-coriander chutney.
benefits: High protein, gluten-free, easily digestible morning breakfast.
tips: Soaking moong dal for 2 hours makes the chillas light and crisp.

name: Jain Chana Sundal (High-Fiber Snack)
recipe: 1. Heat coconut oil, splutter mustard seeds, curry leaves, and hing. 2. Add boiled chana and toss with salt and turmeric for 2 mins. 3. Garnish with fresh grated coconut and a squeeze of fresh lemon.
benefits: Traditional South Indian temple-style high-protein snack, completely sattvic.
tips: Boil chana in batch and store in fridge for quick 5-min prep.

name: Jain Dahi Bhindi with 2 Phulkas
servingUnit: 1 bowl Dahi Bhindi + 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas
recipe: 1. Saute sliced dry bhindi in oil until non-slimy. 2. Whisk curd with besan and spices. Pour into pan on low flame and simmer 3 mins. 3. Serve hot with 2 fresh phulkas.
benefits: Rich in mucilage fiber for digestion, vitamin C and folate.
tips: Ensure bhindi is completely dry before chopping to prevent slime.

name: Desi Egg Bhurji (3 Eggs) with 2 Phulkas & Salad
servingUnit: 1 bowl 3-Egg Bhurji + 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas + Onion-Tomato Salad
ingredients: Green Chili, Turmeric, Pav Bhaji Masala / Garam Masala
recipe: 1. Saute onion, green chili, and tomato in oil. 2. Whisk 3 whole eggs with salt and turmeric, pour into pan, and scramble on medium heat for 3 mins. 3. Garnish with coriander and serve with 2 warm phulkas.
benefits: Complete amino acid profile, high choline, excellent post-workout repair.
tips: Don't overcook the eggs to keep the bhurji soft and juicy.

name: Homestyle Egg Curry (2 Eggs) with Steamed Rice & Dal
servingUnit: 1 bowl Egg Curry (2 eggs) + 1 cup Steamed Rice + 1 bowl Dal
recipe: 1. Lightly prick and pan-sear boiled eggs. 2. Saute onion, ginger-garlic, tomato, and spices into a thick gravy. 3. Add eggs and simmer with 1/2 cup water. 4. Serve with steamed rice and dal.
benefits: Comfort food classic, balanced macros, sustained glycogen replenishment.
tips: Lightly slit eggs on the sides so the curry gravy penetrates deep inside.

name: 4 Boiled Egg Whites + 1 Whole Egg Chaat Bowl
servingUnit: 1 bowl chopped eggs (4 whites + 1 yolk) + Spices & Lemon
ingredients: Finely chopped Onion, Tomato, Green chili
Chaat Masala, Roasted Cumin, Black Pepper
recipe: 1. Slice boiled eggs into bite-sized cubes. 2. Toss with chopped onion, tomato, green chili, and coriander. 3. Sprinkle chaat masala, cumin powder, black pepper, and fresh lemon juice. Mix gently.
benefits: Lean muscle repair, zero cooking effort if batch boiled, pocket-friendly.
tips: Boil 10 eggs on Sunday night to enjoy quick post-workout fuel throughout the week.

name: Double Egg Masala Omelette with 2 Slices Whole Wheat Toast
servingUnit: 2-Egg Masala Omelette + 2 toasted Whole Wheat Bread slices
recipe: 1. Whisk eggs vigorously with chopped onion, tomato, green chili, coriander, and salt. 2. Pour onto hot pan with 1 tsp butter and cook both sides until golden. 3. Toast bread slices on the side and serve together.
benefits: Quick high-bioavailability breakfast, rich in B-vitamins and lutein.
tips: Add a pinch of turmeric to remove any egg odor.

name: High-Protein Soya Bhurji with 2 Phulkas & Dal
servingUnit: 1 bowl Soya Granule Bhurji + 1 bowl Moong Dal + 2 Phulkas
recipe: 1. Soak soya granules in boiling water for 5 mins, drain and squeeze out all water thoroughly. 2. Saute onion, ginger-garlic, and tomato in mustard oil. 3. Add soya granules, spices, and cook for 5 mins. 4. Serve with 2 phulkas and dal.
benefits: Highest protein-per-rupee in India (52% protein), plant-based muscle builder.
tips: Squeeze out the water completely from soya to ensure it absorbs the curry masala flavor.

name: Tofu Matar Curry with 2 Phulkas & Cucumber Salad
servingUnit: 1 bowl Tofu Matar + 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas + Fresh Salad
recipe: 1. Pan-sear tofu cubes until light golden. 2. Prepare homestyle onion-tomato gravy with ginger-garlic and spices. 3. Add green peas, tofu cubes, and 1/2 cup water; simmer for 5 mins. 4. Serve with 2 fresh phulkas.
benefits: Dairy-free complete plant protein, low saturated fat, rich in isoflavones.
tips: Press tofu in a paper towel before cubing to give it a firmer, paneer-like chew.

name: Kala Chana Curry with Jeera Brown Rice & Kachumber
servingUnit: 1 deep bowl Kala Chana Curry + 1 cup Jeera Rice + Kachumber Salad
recipe: 1. Pressure cook soaked kala chana with tea bag/spices for 5 whistles. 2. Saute onion, ginger-garlic, tomato, and ground spices. 3. Add boiled chana with its dark broth and simmer 8 mins. 4. Serve with jeera rice and fresh kachumber.
benefits: Extremely rich in dietary iron, slow-digesting complex carbs, high satiety.
tips: Mash a few tablespoons of boiled chana to thicken the gravy naturally.

name: Homestyle Chicken Curry (150g Breast) with 2 Phulkas & Salad
servingUnit: 1 bowl Chicken Curry (150g boneless chicken) + 2 Phulkas + Salad
recipe: 1. Marinate chicken with curd, turmeric, and ginger-garlic. 2. Brown sliced onions in oil, add tomato puree and spices. 3. Add chicken pieces and bhunao (saute) on high heat for 5 mins, add water and simmer 10 mins. 4. Serve with 2 phulkas.
benefits: Ultra lean high protein (42g), zero trans-fat, optimal hypertrophy fuel.
tips: Cook chicken breast for only 10-12 mins to maintain tenderness and avoid dryness.

name: Bengali Rohu Fish Curry with Steamed Rice & Green Salad
servingUnit: 2 pieces Fish Curry + 1 cup Steamed Rice + Cucumber salad
ingredients: Turmeric, Cumin powder, Mustard Oil - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Rub fish with salt and turmeric; lightly shallow-fry in mustard oil for 2 mins per side. 2. Temper remaining oil with kalonji and green chili. Add tomato and cumin paste. 3. Add 1 cup water, bring to boil, add fish, and simmer 5 mins. 4. Serve with steamed rice.
benefits: Rich in Omega-3 fatty acids, EPA/DHA for joint health, high digestibility.
tips: Mustard oil is essential for the authentic East Indian flavor profile.

name: Grilled Chicken Tikka Bowl with Mint Chutney & 2 Phulkas
servingUnit: 150g Chicken Tikka + 2 Phulkas + Fresh Mint Chutney + Onion rings
ingredients: Ginger-garlic, Kashmiri Lal Mirch, Chaat Masala
recipe: 1. Marinate chicken cubes in hung curd, ginger-garlic paste, spices, and mustard oil for 20 mins. 2. Pan-grill or air-fry on high heat for 10-12 mins until lightly charred. 3. Serve hot with 2 phulkas and mint chutney.
benefits: Restaurant-quality taste with clean macros and high lean protein.
tips: Use Kashmiri chili powder for bright red color without excessive heat.

name: Moong Dal Pesarattu with Ginger Chutney (2 pieces)
recipe: 1. Grind soaked green moong with ginger, chili, and cumin into a smooth dosa-like batter. 2. Spread thin on hot tawa, top with chopped onion, drizzle oil, and roast crisp. 3. Serve with traditional ginger chutney.
benefits: Whole grain and legume combo, low glycemic index, sustained morning energy.
tips: No fermentation required; batter can be made fresh immediately after soaking.

name: South Indian Sambar Rice with Curd & Boiled Egg / Paneer
servingUnit: 1 deep bowl Sambar Rice + 1 bowl Fresh Curd + 50g Paneer / 2 Eggs
ingredients: Sambar powder, Mustard seeds, Curry leaves, Desi Ghee - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Cook toor dal and rice together until soft. 2. Boil drumstick and vegetables with sambar powder and tamarind extract. 3. Mix dal-rice and vegetables, temper with ghee, mustard, and curry leaves. 4. Serve with curd and paneer/egg.
benefits: Complete amino acid profile, gut-friendly fermented curd accompaniment.
tips: Pressure cook dal and rice together to save 15 minutes of cooking time.

name: Classic Poha with Roasted Peanuts & Curry Leaves
ingredients: Mustard seeds, Green chili, Curry leaves
recipe: 1. Rinse poha in water and drain. 2. Roast peanuts in oil until crunchy. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chili, and onion; saute 3 mins. 3. Add turmeric, salt, and drained poha. Toss gently for 2 mins on low heat. 4. Squeeze fresh lemon.
benefits: Light, easily digestible, natural source of iron and carbohydrates.
tips: Do not soak poha in water; a quick rinse in a colander keeps it fluffy.

name: Besan Chilla with Paneer & Green Chutney (2 pieces)
servingUnit: 2 Besan Chillas stuffed with 50g grated Paneer + Mint Chutney
ingredients: Onion, Tomato, Green chili - finely chopped
recipe: 1. Whisk besan with water, ajwain, chopped veggies, and spices into a pouring batter. 2. Cook on hot tawa until crisp, spread grated paneer in the center, and fold. 3. Serve with mint chutney.
benefits: High plant + dairy protein synergy, rich in zinc and folate.
tips: Ajwain enhances digestion and imparts classic aroma to besan.

name: Steamed Idli (3 pieces) with Sambar & Coconut Chutney
servingUnit: 3 soft Idlis + 1 bowl Sambar + 1 tbsp Coconut Chutney
recipe: 1. Pour batter into greased idli molds and steam for 10 mins. 2. Serve steaming hot with vegetable toor dal sambar and fresh coconut chutney.
benefits: Naturally fermented for optimal gut microbiome, zero added fat in idli.
tips: Ferment batter overnight in a warm spot for the softest idlis.

name: Stuffed Paneer Paratha (1 large) with Curd & Pickle
servingUnit: 1 large stuffed Paratha + 1 cup fresh Dahi
ingredients: Green chili, Coriander, Ajwain, Garam Masala
recipe: 1. Stuff seasoned grated paneer inside rolled atta dough. 2. Gently roll into a thick paratha and roast on tawa with 1 tsp ghee until golden spots appear. 3. Serve hot with chilled dahi.
benefits: Long-lasting morning satiety, sustained amino acid release from paneer.
tips: Ensure grated paneer has no excess moisture before stuffing to prevent tearing.

name: Rolled Oats Vegetable Upma with Roasted Peanuts
ingredients: Mustard seeds, Green chili, Curry leaves
recipe: 1. Dry roast oats for 2 mins and set aside. 2. Saute mustard seeds, peanuts, curry leaves, and veggies in oil until tender. 3. Add 1.25 cups water and salt, bring to boil, stir in roasted oats, and cook 3 mins.
benefits: Beta-glucan soluble fiber for cholesterol reduction and steady blood glucose.
tips: Roasting the oats first keeps the upma grain-separated and non-sticky.

name: Classic Rajma Masala with Steamed Basmati Rice & Curd
servingUnit: 1 deep bowl Rajma Curry + 1 cup Steamed Rice + 1 bowl Dahi + Onion rings
ingredients: Kashmiri Lal Mirch, Garam Masala, Kasuri Methi
recipe: 1. Pressure cook soaked rajma with whole spices for 5 whistles until melt-in-mouth soft. 2. Saute onion-tomato-ginger paste with spices until oil separates. 3. Add rajma and simmer 10 mins. 4. Serve with steamed rice and curd.
benefits: Iconic North Indian complete protein combination, high soluble fiber.
tips: Soak rajma for 8 hours in warm water to ensure uniform, creamy cooking.

name: Dal Tadka with 2 Phulkas, Bhindi Sabzi & Curd Thali
servingUnit: 1 bowl Dal Tadka + 1 bowl Bhindi Masala + 2 Phulkas + 1 cup Curd
ingredients: Cumin, Garlic, Dry Red Chili, Hing, Turmeric
recipe: 1. Pressure cook dal with turmeric and salt. 2. Fry bhindi with spices in minimal oil. 3. Give dal a smoking ghee tadka with cumin, garlic, and dry red chili. 4. Serve with 2 fresh phulkas and curd.
benefits: Balanced Indian household staples, complete amino acid complementation.
tips: Use a mix of toor and moong dal for optimal creaminess and lightness.

name: Palak Paneer with 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas & Salad
servingUnit: 1 bowl Palak Paneer (120g paneer) + 2 Phulkas + Cucumber-Tomato Salad
ingredients: Garam Masala, Kasuri Methi, Green Chili
recipe: 1. Blanch spinach in boiling water for 2 mins and immediately ice-bath to preserve vibrant green color. Puree smooth. 2. Saute onion-ginger-garlic, add spinach puree, spices, and cubed paneer. 3. Simmer 3 mins and serve with phulkas.
benefits: High iron, lutein, calcium, and complete milk protein.
tips: Blanching palak for only 2 mins keeps the bright emerald green color intact.

name: Chana Masala with 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas & Dahi
servingUnit: 1 bowl Chana Masala + 2 Phulkas + 1 cup Curd + Onion salad
recipe: 1. Pressure cook soaked chana until tender. 2. Saute onion-tomato-ginger paste with chana masala and amchur. 3. Add boiled chickpeas with cooking water, lightly mash some chickpeas to thicken, and simmer 6 mins. 4. Serve with phulkas and curd.
benefits: Rich in zinc, slow-release carbohydrates, high fiber for gut health.
tips: Mashing a few tablespoons of boiled chana gives a restaurant-thick gravy without heavy cream.

name: Hyderabadi Veg Soya Biryani with Cucumber Raita
servingUnit: 1 deep plate Biryani + 1 cup Cucumber-Mint Raita
ingredients: Biryani Spices (Shahi Jeera, Cardamom, Clove, Cinnamon)
recipe: 1. Boil and squeeze soya chunks; marinate in curd, mint, coriander, and biryani spices. 2. Half-cook basmati rice with whole spices. 3. Layer soya masala and rice, seal with lid, and dum-cook for 10 mins. 4. Serve with fresh raita.
benefits: High protein festive dinner with lean macros and authentic spices.
tips: Dum-cooking on low flame allows rice to absorb the spicy soya marinade aroma.

name: Dal Makhani (Low-Fat Homestyle) with 2 Phulkas & Salad
servingUnit: 1 bowl Dal Makhani + 2 Phulkas + Cucumber-Onion Salad
recipe: 1. Slow-cook black urad and rajma until ultra creamy. 2. Saute tomato puree, ginger-garlic, and kashmiri mirch in ghee. 3. Add cooked dal, mash gently, simmer on low heat for 15 mins. Stir in low-fat milk for richness without heavy cream. 4. Serve with phulkas.
benefits: Authentic rich flavor with 70% less fat than restaurant dal makhani.
tips: Low and slow simmering creates natural creaminess from the black lentils.

name: Bihari Sattu Sharbat (50g Sattu with Lemon, Jeera & Mint)
recipe: 1. Add sattu flour to a glass. 2. Pour chilled water while stirring to prevent lumps. 3. Add lemon juice, roasted cumin powder, black salt, and chopped mint. Stir well.
benefits: Desi natural protein shake, cooling electrolytes, zero sugar, high satiety.
tips: Whisk with a fork or shaker bottle for a lump-free smooth drink.

name: Whey Protein Shake with Banana & Milk (High-Recovery)
recipe: 1. Blend whey protein, toned milk, and banana in a blender or shake vigorously in a shaker bottle for 30 seconds. 2. Drink immediately post workout.
benefits: Rapid leucine delivery for maximal muscle protein synthesis, quick glycogen refill.
tips: Using cold milk creates a thick, milkshake-like texture.

name: Sprouted Moong & Kala Chana Chaat (High-Fiber Snack)
ingredients: Green Chili, Fresh Coriander, Chaat Masala
recipe: 1. Steam sprouted moong and chana for 3 mins (or use raw). 2. Toss with chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili, and fresh coriander. 3. Season with chaat masala and fresh lemon juice.
benefits: Living enzymes, bioavailable vitamin C, and prebiotic fiber.
tips: Sprouting pulses doubles their antioxidant and vitamin C content.

name: Roasted Makhana (Foxnuts) with Ghee & Rock Salt
ingredients: Rock Salt (Sendha Namak), Black Pepper, Turmeric - pinch
recipe: 1. Heat 1 tsp ghee in a heavy kadai. 2. Add makhana and slow roast on low flame for 5-6 mins until crisp. 3. Sprinkle rock salt and freshly cracked black pepper. Toss well.
benefits: Low glycemic index, rich in magnesium and antioxidants, light on stomach.
tips: Roast on low heat; high heat burns the outer shell while leaving the core chewy.

name: Banana (1 medium)
recipe: Peel and eat as is, or slice into a bowl.
benefits: Rich in potassium, natural sugars for quick energy, and prebiotic fiber.
tips: Eat pre-workout for a quick energy boost. Pair with peanut butter for sustained energy.

name: Apple (1 medium)
recipe: Wash and eat whole, or slice and serve.
benefits: High in quercetin, catechin, and pectin fiber. Supports gut health.
tips: Eat with skin on for maximum fiber and polyphenol content.

name: Mango (1 cup sliced)
recipe: Peel the mango and slice the flesh away from the seed. Serve chilled.
benefits: Rich in Vitamin C, beta-carotene, and digestive enzymes like amylase.
tips: Best consumed in the morning or pre-workout. Avoid at night for weight loss goals.

name: Papaya (1 cup)
recipe: Scoop out seeds, peel the skin, and cube the flesh.
benefits: Contains papain enzyme for protein digestion. Excellent for gut health and immunity.
tips: Eat on an empty stomach in the morning for best digestive benefits.

name: Guava (1 medium)
recipe: Wash, remove ends, and eat whole or cut into slices. Sprinkle chaat masala if preferred.
benefits: Exceptionally high in Vitamin C (4× an orange). High fiber aids digestion.
tips: Eat with the seeds for maximum fiber. Excellent for diabetics due to low GI.

name: Pomegranate (1/2 cup seeds)
recipe: Score the pomegranate, break it open underwater to avoid staining, and collect the seeds.
benefits: Powerful antioxidant. Reduces inflammation and supports heart health.
tips: Add to curd, salads, or chaats for flavor and nutrition boost.

name: Dates (3 pieces)
recipe: Remove pits and eat as is, or stuff with nut butter.
benefits: Natural source of iron, potassium, and quick-release carbohydrates for energy.
tips: Excellent pre-workout natural energy source. Avoid in large quantities for diabetics.

name: Mixed Nuts — 30g
recipe: Measure and eat as is.
benefits: Healthy omega-3 and omega-6 fats, vitamin E, magnesium. Supports brain and heart health.
tips: Soak almonds and walnuts overnight for better mineral absorption. Keep cashews raw.

name: Peanuts — Roasted Plain (30g)
recipe: Eat as is, or season with salt and lime.
benefits: High protein plant-based snack. Rich in niacin and resveratrol.
tips: Budget-friendly protein source. Avoid salted versions for sodium-conscious users.

name: Walnuts
recipe: Eat as raw snack or add to oatmeal and bowls.
benefits: Richest plant source of omega-3 (ALA). Supports cognitive function and reduces inflammation.
tips: Soak in water overnight to reduce phytic acid and improve digestion.

name: Banana & Dates Pre-Workout Snack
ingredients: Medjool or Deglet dates - 3 pieces pitted (40g)
recipe: 1. Peel the banana. 2. Remove pits from dates if not pre-pitted. 3. Eat together 30–45 minutes before training.
benefits: Natural simple sugars from banana and dates provide rapid blood glucose for immediate pre-workout energy without any digestive discomfort. Potassium in banana prevents muscle cramps during training.
tips: Best consumed 30–45 minutes before workouts under 75 minutes. For longer sessions, pair with a sattu drink for sustained energy.

name: Poha Chivda with Roasted Peanuts
ingredients: Salt and lemon juice to taste
recipe: 1. Dry roast thin poha in a kadai on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until crispy. 2. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and turmeric. 3. Toss in roasted peanuts. 4. Finish with lemon juice and salt.
benefits: Thin poha is light on digestion — ideal 45–60 minutes before training. Peanuts add protein and healthy fats for sustained energy without GI heaviness.
tips: Can be made in bulk and stored in an airtight container for 5 days. Naturally gluten-free and vegan.

name: Coconut Water with Soaked Almonds
ingredients: Fresh coconut water - 250ml (or packaged, no sugar added)
Raw almonds - 8 pieces (soaked overnight, skin removed)
recipe: 1. Soak almonds overnight in water. 2. Remove skin by pinching each almond. 3. Drink coconut water and eat soaked almonds together before training.
benefits: Coconut water provides natural electrolytes (potassium 600mg, magnesium, sodium) for hydration and cramp prevention. Soaking removes phytic acid from almonds for better mineral absorption.
tips: One of the best hydrating pre-workout options especially in Indian summers. Avoid if allergic to tree nuts. Choose packaged coconut water with no added sugar.

name: Ragi Mudde with Sambar (South Indian Pre-Workout)
servingUnit: 2 ragi mudde balls (60g ragi flour) + 1 cup sambar (200ml)
ingredients: Vegetable sambar - 1 cup (200ml, homemade or packet)
recipe: 1. Bring 200ml salted water to a rolling boil. 2. Reduce heat to low. 3. Add ragi flour gradually while stirring constantly to prevent lumps. 4. Cook on low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring continuously, until the mass thickens and pulls cleanly away from the pan sides. 5. Shape into smooth balls using wet hands. 6. Serve immediately with hot sambar.
benefits: Ragi is among the richest cereal sources of calcium (344mg/100g) and iron. Its complex carbohydrates digest slowly, providing sustained energy for 2–3 hours of training without blood sugar spikes. Naturally gluten-free.
tips: Traditional South Indian pre-activity staple eaten by farmers and athletes for centuries. Eat 60 minutes before training for best results. Ragi mudde hardens when cold — eat immediately after preparation.

name: Bajra Roti with Jaggery & Ghee
servingUnit: 2 bajra rotis (60g flour) + 1 tsp ghee + 10g jaggery
ingredients: Warm water - as needed to knead
recipe: 1. Knead bajra flour with warm water into a soft pliable dough (no resting needed). 2. Divide into 2 equal portions. 3. Flatten each into a thick roti (0.5cm) by patting with hands — bajra dough does not roll easily with a belan. 4. Cook on a hot dry tawa until dark spots appear on both sides (2-3 min per side). 5. Serve immediately topped with 1/2 tsp ghee each and small pieces of jaggery.
benefits: Bajra is rich in magnesium, phosphorus, and B-complex vitamins essential for energy metabolism. The jaggery provides natural iron and immediate glucose. Traditional Rajasthani pre-activity fuel consumed by farmers and wrestlers for generations.
tips: Bajra roti must be eaten hot — it becomes very hard and dry when cold. The ghee provides fat-soluble vitamins. Best consumed 45–60 minutes before moderate-to-heavy training sessions.

name: Kolkata Dim Kosha with 2 Atta Rotis
ingredients: Turmeric, red chili & garam masala - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Lightly slit boiled eggs, toss with turmeric and salt, pan-sear in 1/2 tsp mustard oil until golden. 2. In same pan, add onions and brown slowly. 3. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and spices; sauté till oil separates. 4. Add 1/2 cup warm water and simmer into a rich gravy. 5. Add seared eggs, simmer 3 minutes. 6. Serve hot with 2 freshly rolled atta rotis.
benefits: High biological value protein with choline and lutein from eggs for cognitive performance and lean muscle preservation.
tips: Sauté onions slowly on medium heat to develop rich Bengali kosha flavor without excess oil.

name: Traditional Bengali Macher Jhol with Steamed Rice
ingredients: Basmati / Gobindobhog rice - 50g raw (1 cup cooked)
recipe: 1. Marinate fish with turmeric and rock salt; lightly sear in mustard oil for 2 minutes each side. 2. Temper oil with nigella seeds and green chilies. 3. Add cumin paste, turmeric, and potato slices. 4. Pour 1.5 cups water and bring to a simmer. 5. Add fish steaks and simmer on low for 6 minutes until tender. 6. Serve alongside 1 cup steamed rice.
benefits: Lean freshwater fish provides omega-3 fatty acids (EPA & DHA) which reduce exercise-induced inflammation and support cardiovascular health.
tips: Light stewing preserves the delicate fish protein and keeps the broth easy on digestion.
servingUnit: 1 Fish Steak in Broth + 1 Cup Rice

name: Bengali Cholar Dal with Grated Coconut & 2 Phulkas
recipe: 1. Pressure cook chana dal with turmeric, bay leaf, and water for 4 whistles. 2. Heat mustard oil, add cumin seeds, hing, dry red chili, and coconut slices. Fry until coconut turns golden brown. 3. Add ginger paste and sauté 1 minute. 4. Pour in boiled dal, simmer 5 minutes until thick and creamy. 5. Serve with 2 warm whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: Chana dal has one of the lowest glycemic indices among pulses (GI ~28), delivering sustained glycogen release and high fiber.
tips: Roasting fresh coconut slices in the tempering gives authentic Bengali sweetness without added refined sugar.

name: Bhaja Moong Dal Khichuri with Roasted Begun Bhaja
recipe: 1. Dry roast moong dal until aromatic and golden. Wash with rice. 2. In a pressure cooker, temper mustard oil with cumin, bay leaf, and ginger. 3. Add roasted dal and rice, stir 1 minute. 4. Add 3 cups water, turmeric, and salt; cook for 3 whistles until soft. 5. Rub eggplant slices with turmeric and salt; pan-sear in 1/2 tsp oil until tender. 6. Serve khichuri with seared begun bhaja.
benefits: Roasting moong dal breaks down complex starches for ultra-gentle gastric emptying and complete amino acid profile with rice.
tips: Pan-sear eggplant with a non-stick pan to use minimal mustard oil while keeping it crisp on the outside.
servingUnit: 1 Deep Bowl Khichuri + 2 Begun Bhaja Slices

name: Kolkata Street-Style Ghugni Chaat with Chopped Salad
ingredients: Dried yellow / white peas (motor suti) - 60g raw (boiled)
recipe: 1. Soak dried yellow peas overnight and boil with salt and turmeric until tender. 2. Warm boiled peas in their broth with bhaja masala. 3. Spoon into a bowl, top with chopped raw onion, tomato, green chilies, and fresh coriander. 4. Squeeze generous fresh lemon juice and toss thoroughly.
benefits: Dried yellow peas are rich in soluble prebiotic fiber and complex starch, supporting gut microbiome and zero GI lag.
tips: Bhaja masala (dry roasted cumin, dry red chili, and coriander seeds ground coarse) gives genuine Kolkata flavor.

name: High-Protein Bengali Mishti Doi (Stevia & Whey Infused)
ingredients: Whey protein vanilla or unflavored - 15g (half scoop)
recipe: 1. In a small earthen bowl, whisk hung curd with cardamom powder and saffron until silky smooth. 2. Whisk in whey protein powder until completely blended with no lumps. 3. Swirl in 1 tsp natural date syrup or stevia for signature caramelized earthen tang. 4. Chill for 30 minutes and enjoy.
benefits: Delivers 26g of bioavailable casein and whey protein along with live probiotic Lactobacillus cultures for gut barrier integrity.
tips: Use an earthen clay cup (matka) for authentic Bengali earthen aroma.

name: Bengali Sorshe Shorshe Paneer with Steamed Gobindobhog Rice
ingredients: Yellow and black mustard paste - 1 tbsp
recipe: 1. Blend yellow and black mustard seeds with green chili and salt into a fine paste. 2. Heat 1 tsp mustard oil, add mustard paste, turmeric, and 1/2 cup warm water. 3. Bring to gentle simmer. 4. Add fresh paneer cubes and slit green chili. 5. Simmer 3 minutes on low covered. 6. Serve with hot steamed rice.
benefits: Mustard seeds contain glucosinolates and allyl isothiocyanate which stimulate digestive enzymes and boost resting metabolic rate.
tips: Use yellow mustard seeds to avoid excess bitterness.

name: Methi Thepla with Fresh Spiced Curd (3 Theplas)
ingredients: Fresh fenugreek leaves (methi) - 1/2 cup finely chopped
recipe: 1. Knead atta, besan, washed chopped methi leaves, ajwain, sesame seeds, turmeric, and 2 tbsp curd into a soft pliable dough. 2. Roll into 3 thin theplas. 3. Cook on a hot tawa with minimal oil brushing until light brown spots appear. 4. Serve with 100g chilled fresh curd sprinkled with roasted cumin.
benefits: Fenugreek (methi) is rich in 4-hydroxyisoleucine which enhances insulin sensitivity, slows glucose absorption, and stabilizes morning glycemia.
tips: Ajwain and sesame seeds add essential minerals (calcium & magnesium) and prevent morning bloating.

name: Gujarati Khatta Moong (Sprouted Moong in Buttermilk Gravy) with 2 Phulkas
ingredients: Mustard seeds, cumin & curry leaves - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Steam sprouted green moong for 6 minutes. 2. Whisk buttermilk with besan, turmeric, and salt. 3. Heat 1/2 tsp oil, temper with mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves, and ginger-chili paste. 4. Pour buttermilk mixture and simmer while stirring continuously until it thickens. 5. Add steamed moong, simmer 4 minutes. 6. Serve with 2 warm phulkas.
benefits: Sprouting multiplies moong protein bioavailability and reduces phytates, while buttermilk provides probiotics and tart lactic acid for gut flora.
tips: Whisk besan thoroughly into buttermilk before cooking to prevent curd from splitting.

name: Traditional Gujarati Handvo (Baked Vegetable Lentil Cake)
ingredients: Handvo flour mix (rice, chana dal, toor dal, urad dal) - 60g fermented batter
recipe: 1. Mix fermented lentil-rice batter with grated bottle gourd, ginger-chili paste, turmeric, and salt. 2. Heat 1 tsp oil in a heavy pan, add mustard seeds, sesame seeds, and curry leaves. 3. Pour batter, cover, and cook on low flame for 10 minutes until bottom crust is golden and crisp. 4. Flip carefully and crisp the other side. 5. Slice and serve hot with green mint chutney.
benefits: Four-lentil fermented matrix supplies complete branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) with high dietary fiber and zero wheat.
tips: Grated bottle gourd keeps the handvo moist and nutrient dense while cutting caloric density.

name: Steamed High-Protein Khaman Dhokla with Green Chutney
recipe: 1. Whisk besan with water, lemon juice, ginger-chili paste, turmeric, and salt into a smooth batter. 2. Stir in fruit salt, pour into a greased steaming tray immediately. 3. Steam on high for 15 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. 4. Prepare tempering in 1 tsp oil with mustard seeds, slit chilies, curry leaves, and 1/4 cup water. 5. Pour over steamed dhokla, cut into squares and serve.
benefits: Steamed preparation with zero frying delivers high bioavailable plant protein with negligible saturated fat, making it an ideal pre-workout fuel.
tips: Avoid sugar in the tempering water for a clean fitness formulation.

name: Gujarati Kathol (Sprouted Vaal / Field Bean Curry) with 2 Phulkas
recipe: 1. Boil sprouted vaal with salt and kokum until tender. 2. Heat oil, add ajwain, mustard seeds, hing, and curry leaves. 3. Add vaal with cooking water, coriander-cumin powder, turmeric, and red chili. 4. Simmer 8 minutes until gravy is thick. 5. Serve with 2 soft whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: Vaal beans provide sustained starch digestion, high resistant starch to nourish colonocytes, and substantial vegetable protein.
tips: Ajwain and hing in the tempering eliminate gas and digestive discomfort from field beans.

name: Gujarati Moong Khichdi with Roasted Papad & Curd
recipe: 1. Wash moong dal with skin and rice together. 2. In pressure cooker, heat 1 tsp ghee, add cumin seeds and 2 cloves. 3. Add dal, rice, turmeric, salt, and 3 cups water. 4. Pressure cook for 4 whistles until soft and porridge-like. 5. Serve with 100g fresh dahi and 1 dry-roasted papad.
benefits: Green split moong retains dietary fiber from the husk, delivering gentle digestive transit and complete protein recovery.
tips: Green moong dal with skin provides twice the fiber of dehusked yellow dal.

name: Maharashtrian Kanda Poha with Peanuts & Boiled Sprouts
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves & green chili - 1 tsp
Turmeric, salt & fresh lemon juice - to taste
recipe: 1. Rinse poha in a colander for 30 seconds, drain and rest 5 minutes. 2. Heat oil, fry peanuts until crunchy, remove half for topping. 3. In same oil, crackle mustard seeds, curry leaves, and sauté onions with green chili. 4. Add turmeric, salt, boiled sprouts, and drained poha. 5. Steam covered on low for 2 minutes. 6. Garnish with lemon juice and crunchy peanuts.
benefits: Iron-fortified flattened rice pairs with lemon juice (Vitamin C) for maximum non-heme iron absorption, supporting oxygen delivery during workouts.
tips: Rinse poha gently without mashing to keep every flake separate and fluffy.

name: Pithla with Jowar Bhakri & Thecha (Maharashtrian High-Fiber Thali)
recipe: 1. Whisk besan with water, turmeric, and salt into a smooth slurry. 2. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves, garlic, and onions; sauté until translucent. 3. Pour besan slurry, stirring vigorously to avoid lumps. Cook covered 5 minutes until thick. 4. Knead jowar flour with warm water, pat into a thin round bhakri, and roast on tawa with water wash. 5. Serve hot pithla with jowar bhakri and garlic thecha.
benefits: Sorghum (jowar) is naturally gluten-free and packed with polyphenols, resistant starch, and low glycemic load for long-term cardiometabolic health.
tips: Use warm water to knead jowar flour to make the bhakri pliable and soft without cracking.

name: Sprouted Matki (Moth Bean) Usal with 2 Phulkas
ingredients: Kanda-lasun masala or goda masala - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Steam sprouted matki for 5 minutes. 2. Heat oil, temper with mustard and cumin seeds. 3. Add onions, tomatoes, and goda masala; sauté until soft. 4. Add steamed matki and 1/2 cup water. Simmer covered for 6 minutes. 5. Squeeze fresh lemon juice, garnish with coriander, and serve with 2 warm phulkas.
benefits: Moth beans are an arid super-legume with high zinc, iron, and potassium levels, supporting cellular repair and electrolyte replenishment.
tips: Sprouting moth beans doubles their bioavailable vitamin C and enzymatic activity.

name: Kolhapuri High-Protein Soya Bhurji with 2 Jowar Bhakris
recipe: 1. Boil soya granules in salted water for 5 minutes, rinse and squeeze out excess water completely. 2. Heat oil, add onions, ginger-garlic paste, and sauté until golden brown. 3. Add tomatoes and spicy Kolhapuri masala; cook until pulpy. 4. Stir in soya granules, sauté on high heat for 4 minutes to absorb flavors. 5. Serve with 2 fresh jowar bhakris and lemon wedges.
benefits: Delivers 34g of complete plant protein with all essential amino acids, meeting the high leucine threshold for muscle protein synthesis.
tips: Squeezing out soya water thoroughly removes the earthy soy taste and allows Kolhapuri spices to penetrate.

name: Rajasthani Gatte ki Sabzi with 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas
ingredients: Ajwain, cumin & crushed coriander seeds - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Knead besan with ajwain, turmeric, chili, 1 tsp curd, and water into a stiff dough. 2. Roll into cylinders, boil in bubbling water for 8 minutes until gatte float, slice into bite-sized rounds. 3. Whisk remaining curd with spices. 4. In a pan, heat 1 tsp oil with cumin and hing, pour spiced curd, stirring continuously to prevent curdling. 5. Add boiled gatte pieces and simmer 6 minutes. 6. Serve with 2 phulkas.
benefits: Besan dumplings in a spiced probiotic curd reduction deliver plant-dairy protein complementarity without processed ingredients.
tips: Keep the water used to boil gatte and use it as gravy base for maximum flavor and nutrition.

name: Rajasthani Bajra Roti with Spiced Kadhi & Fresh Curd
ingredients: Desi ghee - 1/2 tsp for roti brush
Mustard seeds, cumin & methi seeds - 1/2 tsp
recipe: 1. Whisk buttermilk with besan, turmeric, and ginger-chili paste. 2. Temper with mustard seeds, cumin, fenugreek seeds, and hing. Simmer kadhi for 10 minutes until aromatic. 3. Knead bajra flour with warm water, pat into a thick round roti on a tawa, roast until crisp and puffed. 4. Brush with 1/2 tsp pure ghee and serve alongside piping hot kadhi.
benefits: Pearl millet (bajra) is high in slowly digestible starch and iron, keeping you energized for hours and regulating winter body thermogenesis.
tips: Bajra roti is best consumed fresh and hot directly off the tawa.

name: Fitness Oven-Baked Dal Baati (Single Baati Fitness Portion) with Yellow Dal
ingredients: Desi ghee - 1 tsp (measured dip, not drowned)
recipe: 1. Knead coarse wheat flour, rava, ajwain, pinch soda, and water into a firm dough ball. 2. Bake in preheated oven or air fryer at 180°C for 22 minutes until crusty and cracked. 3. Pressure cook mixed dal with turmeric and salt. 4. Temper dal with cumin, hing, and green chilies. 5. Crack open hot baked baati, brush with 1 measured tsp desi ghee, and serve with piping hot dal.
benefits: Traditional baked whole wheat baati provides long-burning complex energy without deep frying, while mixed lentils supply complete amino acids.
tips: Baking or air-frying baati saves over 250 kcal of submerged frying oil while retaining the authentic crust.

name: Overnight Rolled Oats with Chia Seeds, Whey & Sliced Banana
recipe: 1. In a jar or container, mix rolled oats, chia seeds, cinnamon, and whey protein. 2. Pour in 180ml cold toned milk or water and stir thoroughly. 3. Cover and place in the refrigerator overnight (or rest 15 minutes). 4. Top with sliced banana rounds and enjoy instantly.
benefits: Soluble beta-glucan fiber in oats forms a gentle gel with chia seeds that slows glucose uptake, while whey delivers 30g fast amino acids.
tips: Zero cooking required. Make 3 jars at once on Sunday for grab-and-go morning breakfasts.

name: Sprouted Moong & Pomegranate Protein Chaat (No-Cook Bowl)
recipe: 1. In a bowl, toss sprouted raw green moong with diced cucumber and ruby pomegranate arils. 2. Season with chaat masala, roasted cumin, and black salt. 3. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the bowl and toss evenly. Serve immediately.
benefits: Enzyme-rich raw sprouted legumes provide active vitamins C & K, high folate, and zero added cooking oil.
tips: Pomegranate adds natural sweetness and potent polyphenols for endothelial nitric oxide production.

name: Greek Yogurt Protein Crunch Bowl with Almonds & Flaxseeds
ingredients: Plain unsweetened Greek yogurt (or hung curd) - 200g
Cardamom or cinnamon powder - a pinch
recipe: 1. Spoon 200g dense Greek yogurt into a bowl. 2. Sprinkle cardamom powder and drizzle a few drops of stevia/honey. 3. Top with crisp apple cubes, chopped crunchy almonds, and roasted flaxseeds. Enjoy immediately.
benefits: High protein density with 24g pure micellar casein and whey, coupled with ALA omega-3s from flaxseeds and vitamin E from almonds.
tips: Dense Greek yogurt contains double the protein of regular curd with half the whey liquid.

name: Natural Peanut Butter Whole Wheat Toast with Fresh Fruit
ingredients: 100% pure natural peanut butter (no added sugar/oil) - 24g (1.5 tbsp)
recipe: 1. Take 2 fresh slices of whole wheat bread. 2. Spread natural unsweetened peanut butter evenly across both slices. 3. Top with banana rounds or thinly sliced apple. 4. Sprinkle chia seeds and enjoy.
benefits: Monounsaturated oleic fats from peanuts provide steady energy release without triggering insulin spikes.
tips: Select single-ingredient peanut butter containing only 100% roasted peanuts.

name: Spiced Low-Fat Paneer Salad Cubes with Chaat Masala & Lemon
recipe: 1. Cut fresh soft low-fat paneer into 1-inch bite-sized cubes. 2. Place in a bowl with diced cucumber and torn mint leaves. 3. Dust with chaat masala, freshly cracked black pepper, and rock salt. 4. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over top, toss gently and enjoy.
benefits: Zero cooking required. Supplies 22g of slow-digesting casein protein, ideal for evening satiety or low-carb fueling.
tips: Soak paneer in warm water for 2 minutes before cubing to make it extra soft without frying.

name: Roasted Chana, Peanuts & Makhana Trail Mix with Lemon Tea
ingredients: Roasted yellow chana (bhuna chana with skin) - 30g
Rock salt & chaat masala - to taste
recipe: 1. In a snack bowl or portable container, mix roasted chana, roasted peanuts, and crunchy makhana. 2. Season with rock salt and chaat masala. 3. Enjoy crunchy dry trail mix alongside a refreshing cup of green tea.
benefits: High dietary fiber and resistant starch from roasted chana keep blood glucose steady and curb mid-afternoon hunger.
tips: Keep a batch in an airtight jar on your desk for zero-effort, clean snacking.

name: Jain Moong Dal Khichdi with Dahi & Roasted Cumin
recipe: 1. Wash moong dal and rice together. 2. Heat 1 tsp ghee in pressure cooker, add cumin seeds, hing, and slit green chili (strictly zero onion, garlic, or ginger). 3. Add dal, rice, turmeric, salt, and 3 cups water. 4. Pressure cook for 3 whistles until soft. 5. Serve with 100g fresh dahi.
benefits: Gentle on digestion, satvik, adhering strictly to Jain dietary principles while supplying complete vegetarian protein.
tips: Use generous hing in the ghee tempering for rich aroma without onions or garlic.

name: Jain Paneer Bhurji with 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas
recipe: 1. Heat 1 tsp oil/ghee, add cumin seeds and hing. 2. Add diced tomatoes, capsicum, and green chili (strictly no onion or garlic). Cook until tomatoes soften. 3. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt. 4. Fold in crumbled fresh paneer and cook on medium flame for 3 minutes. 5. Serve hot with 2 soft whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: High bioavailable protein and essential fats from fresh paneer, with antioxidants from tomatoes and crunchy capsicum.
tips: Capsicum adds crunch and vibrant micronutrients to replace onion texture in Jain recipes.

name: Jain Dal Tadka with Steamed Basmati Rice & Cucumber Salad
ingredients: Cumin seeds, mustard seeds & hing - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Pressure cook toor dal with chopped tomatoes, turmeric, and salt for 4 whistles. Whisk smooth. 2. In a small pan, heat ghee, add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, hing, and slit green chili. 3. Pour crackling tadka over hot boiled dal. 4. Serve with 1 cup steamed basmati rice and crisp cucumber slices.
benefits: Classic comforting comfort meal with balanced carbohydrates and essential amino acids, fully Jain compliant.
tips: Cooking tomatoes inside the dal adds natural tartness and eliminates need for onion gravy.
servingUnit: 1 Bowl Jain Dal + 1 Cup Rice + Cucumber

name: Bihari Sattu Buttermilk Protein Shake (50g Pure Sattu)
recipe: 1. In a tall shaker or glass, add 50g roasted chana sattu flour. 2. Pour 250ml chilled buttermilk. 3. Add black salt, roasted cumin powder, and fresh lemon juice. 4. Shake or whisk vigorously until smooth and frothy. Drink chilled.
benefits: India’s ultimate natural protein shake: 21g protein under ₹15, loaded with cooling electrolytes and insoluble fiber.
tips: Whisk sattu with a little buttermilk first to form a paste before adding remaining liquid to avoid lumps.

name: Homestyle Egg Curry (3 Eggs) with Steamed Rice
recipe: 1. Peel boiled eggs, prick lightly with fork, and pan-sear in 1/2 tsp oil with turmeric for 2 minutes. 2. Sauté onions in remaining oil until golden brown. 3. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and dry spices; cook until oil glazes the edges. 4. Add 3/4 cup water, simmer to a rich curry. 5. Add seared eggs, simmer 4 minutes. 6. Serve with 1 cup hot steamed rice.
benefits: Cost-effective complete protein powerhouse: delivers all 9 essential amino acids, choline, and vitamin B12 for less than ₹35.
tips: Hard boil eggs in advance and store in fridge to cut cooking time to 12 minutes on busy weeknights.

name: Kala Chana Masala Bowl with 2 Phulkas & Kachumber Salad
ingredients: Desi black chickpeas (kala chana) - 60g raw (soaked overnight)
recipe: 1. Pressure cook soaked kala chana with salt and water for 6 whistles until soft. 2. Heat oil, add cumin, sauté onions, ginger, and green chilies. 3. Add tomatoes and chana masala; cook until pulpy. 4. Add boiled chickpeas with their cooking broth; simmer 8 minutes. 5. Serve with 2 whole wheat phulkas and fresh kachumber salad.
benefits: Desi black chickpeas are exceptionally high in dietary iron, insoluble fiber, and magnesium, promoting insulin sensitivity.
tips: Mash a few boiled chickpeas with the back of the spoon to thicken the gravy naturally without starch.

name: Keto Paneer Bhurji with Steamed Cauliflower Rice
recipe: 1. Grate cauliflower in a food processor into rice-like grains; steam in a pan with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes until tender. 2. In another pan, heat 1 tsp ghee, sauté cumin, onions, green chili, and tomatoes. 3. Add turmeric and salt, fold in crumbled paneer, and sauté on medium heat for 3 minutes. 4. Serve savory paneer bhurji atop warm cauliflower rice.
benefits: Only 8g net carbs with 22g protein and healthy dairy fats, maintaining nutritional ketosis while delivering complete comfort food flavor.
tips: Do not overcook cauliflower rice to prevent it from becoming soggy.

name: Keto Egg White & Whole Egg Spinach Scramble with Butter
recipe: 1. Whisk 2 whole eggs and 2 egg whites with salt and black pepper. 2. Melt butter in a non-stick pan, add green chili and chopped spinach; sauté 1 minute until wilted. 3. Pour whisked eggs, let set for 15 seconds, then scramble gently on low heat until soft curds form. 4. Serve immediately with optional grated cheese.
benefits: Zero carbohydrate load with 24g pure animal protein and bioavailable lutein/zeaxanthin for ocular and metabolic support.
tips: Cooking on low heat keeps the scrambled curds velvety and prevents egg protein from drying out.

name: Andhra High-Protein Pesarattu with Ginger Pachadi & Curd
ingredients: Whole green moong - 60g raw (soaked and ground)
recipe: 1. Blend soaked green moong with ginger, green chilies, cumin, and salt into a smooth batter (no fermentation required). 2. Pour ladleful on hot tawa, spread into a crispy thin dosa, top with chopped onions. 3. Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil, crisp both sides until golden. 4. Serve with 100g fresh curd and spicy ginger pachadi.
benefits: Made with 100% whole green gram, delivering 18g plant protein, zero refined rice, and exceptional satiety.
tips: Whole green moong contains natural mucilage that allows crispy dosas without any rice or urad dal.

name: Steamed Ragi Idlis (3 pieces) with Drumstick Sambar
ingredients: Ragi (finger millet) flour & urad dal batter - 3 idlis (150g)
recipe: 1. Steam fermented ragi-urad batter in idli molds for 10 minutes. 2. Pressure cook toor dal with drumsticks, vegetables, sambar powder, and tamarind water. 3. Temper sambar with mustard seeds and curry leaves. 4. Serve 3 fluffy steamed ragi idlis submerged in hot lentil vegetable sambar.
benefits: Finger millet (ragi) is an ancient grain packed with 344mg calcium per 100g, supporting skeletal bone density and steady glycogen.
tips: Submerging idlis in sambar allows them to soak up vegetable polyphenols and spices.

name: South Indian Curd Rice with Pomegranate, Roasted Mustard & Cucumber
recipe: 1. In a bowl, mash warm cooked rice lightly with a fork, mix with fresh chilled curd and diced cucumber. 2. Heat 1/2 tsp ghee, crackle mustard seeds, curry leaves, grated ginger, and green chili. 3. Pour crackling tadka over curd rice. 4. Fold in ruby pomegranate arils and enjoy chilled.
benefits: Optimal gut microbiome recovery: live probiotic cultures combined with resistant rice starch soothe digestive inflammation.
tips: Mashing the rice slightly while warm makes the curd rice velvety and prevents water separation.

name: Tamil Nadu Vegetable Kurma with 2 Whole Wheat Parottas / Phulkas
ingredients: Mixed vegetables (beans, carrots, peas, potatoes) - 1 cup
Fresh coconut & roasted gram (pottukadalai) paste - 1.5 tbsp
recipe: 1. Grind coconut, roasted gram (chana), fennel seeds, and green chili into a smooth kurma paste. 2. Sauté whole spices, onions, and tomatoes in 1 tsp oil. 3. Add mixed vegetables, kurma paste, turmeric, and 1 cup water. 4. Simmer 10 minutes until vegetables are tender and gravy is fragrant. 5. Serve with 2 soft wheat phulkas.
benefits: Fennel and coconut infusion promotes gastric peristalsis, and roasted gram adds smooth plant-based protein thickness.
tips: Using roasted gram (pottukadalai) thickens the kurma naturally while reducing coconut quantity.

name: Kerala Egg Roast (2 Eggs) with Steamed Red Matta Rice
ingredients: Kerala red matta rice - 50g raw (1 cup cooked)
Black pepper, fennel & garam masala - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. In 1 tsp coconut oil, slowly caramelize sliced onions with curry leaves and green chilies for 8 minutes until deep golden. 2. Add ginger-garlic, tomatoes, crushed black pepper, fennel powder, and garam masala. Cook till pulpy. 3. Toss in boiled eggs, coat in thick onion roast. 4. Serve alongside hearty, nutrient-rich Kerala red matta rice.
benefits: Kerala red matta rice retains its outer bran layer rich in thiamine, magnesium, and dietary fiber, yielding sustained postprandial glucose stability.
tips: Caramelizing onions slowly is the secret to authentic Kerala roast sweetness without sugar.
servingUnit: 2 Eggs in Onion Roast + 1 Cup Matta Rice

name: Maharashtrian Thalipeeth (Multi-Grain Spiced Flatbread) with Curd
ingredients: Thalipeeth bhajani flour (jowar, bajra, chana dal, rice, coriander seeds) - 70g
Desi ghee / oil - 1 tsp for tawa
recipe: 1. Knead bhajani flour with onions, fresh coriander, ajwain, sesame seeds, salt, and warm water into soft dough. 2. Pat dough thin directly on tawa or butter paper, make 3 small steam holes in center. 3. Drizzle 1/2 tsp ghee/oil into holes, cook covered on medium heat until golden crisp on both sides. 4. Serve with 100g fresh curd.
benefits: Traditional multi-grain bhajani combines millets and roasted pulses, optimizing amino acid score and micronutrient diversity.
tips: Making small holes in the center of the thalipeeth ensures even steam circulation and crisp edges.

name: Kolhapuri Chicken Sukka (High-Protein Lean Breast) with 2 Phulkas
recipe: 1. Dry roast grated coconut, sliced onion, and whole spices; grind to coarse Kolhapuri paste. 2. Heat 1 tsp oil, sauté chicken breast cubes on high heat for 3 minutes to sear in moisture. 3. Add spice paste, Kolhapuri masala, and 1/4 cup water. 4. Cook covered for 8 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce coats each piece. 5. Serve with 2 warm whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: High biological value poultry protein (38g) with minimal saturated fat, maximizing anabolic muscle protein synthesis.
tips: Cubing chicken breast evenly ensures fast, tender cooking without drying out.

name: Maharashtrian Varan Bhaat with Desi Ghee, Lemon & Roasted Papad
ingredients: Basmati / Indrayani rice - 50g raw (1 cup cooked)
recipe: 1. Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric and salt until silky soft. 2. Mash cooked dal thoroughly with a traditional ravi / whisk. 3. Serve hot over 1 cup warm steamed Indrayani rice. 4. Top with 1 tsp hot fragrant desi ghee and squeeze of fresh juicy lemon. 5. Enjoy with crisp roasted papad.
benefits: The ultimate comforting digestive reset: pure toor dal and rice provides complete protein that is exceptionally easy on gastric transit.
tips: A squeeze of fresh lemon juice enhances non-heme iron absorption from toor dal by over 300%.
servingUnit: 1 Bowl Varan + 1 Cup Bhaat + Ghee & Papad

name: Gujarati Dal Dhokli (Healthy Whole Wheat Strips in Spiced Dal)
ingredients: Mustard seeds, cumin & curry leaves - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Cook toor dal with peanuts until soft, blend into a thin soup with kokum, turmeric, and jaggery/salt. 2. Knead wheat flour with ajwain into a soft dough, roll thin, cut into diamond dhokli strips. 3. Bring dal soup to a rolling boil, drop wheat dhokli strips one by one so they do not stick. 4. Simmer 10 minutes until dhokli is cooked tender and chewy. 5. Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves. Serve piping hot.
benefits: One-pot complete balanced meal: whole wheat complex starch simmers directly in legume protein broth, creating high satiety.
tips: Add dhokli strips only when dal is vigorously boiling to prevent them from becoming soggy.

name: Gujarati Sev Tameta Nu Shaak (Low-Oil Fitness Version) with 2 Phulkas
ingredients: Ripe juicy red tomatoes - 2 large chopped
recipe: 1. In 1 tsp oil, temper mustard seeds, cumin, hing, and ginger-chili paste. 2. Add chopped ripe tomatoes, turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, and salt. 3. Sauté until tomatoes break down into a luscious gravy with 1/4 cup water. 4. Just before eating, sprinkle crispy sev on top. 5. Serve with 2 hot whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: Cooked tomatoes deliver concentrated lycopene, an antioxidant that protects cellular membranes against oxidative exercise damage.
tips: Keep sev separate and sprinkle immediately before eating to maintain crunch without soggy absorption.

name: Panchmel Dal (5 Lentil Rajasthani Protein Blend) with 2 Phulkas
ingredients: Five lentil blend (moong, chana, toor, masoor, urad) - 55g raw
recipe: 1. Soak five-dal blend for 30 minutes, pressure cook with tomatoes, turmeric, and salt for 4 whistles. 2. Whisk cooked lentils into a thick textured dal. 3. Heat 1 tsp ghee, add cloves, bay leaf, cumin seeds, hing, dry red chili, and ginger. 4. Pour crackling royal tadka over bubbling dal. 5. Serve with 2 whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: Five distinct legumes complement each other’s amino acid deficits, delivering 20g balanced protein and diverse dietary fiber.
tips: A combination of 5 lentils provides better micronutrient diversity than single-pulse preparations.

name: Rajasthani Papad Methi ki Sabzi with 2 Bajra Rotis
ingredients: Roasted urad papad - 2 broken into pieces
Turmeric, amchur (dry mango) & red chili - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Boil soaked fenugreek seeds in water twice to eliminate bitterness. 2. Heat oil, temper with cumin and hing. 3. Add boiled methi dana, spices, amchur powder, and 1/2 cup water. 4. Add broken papad pieces and simmer for 3 minutes until papad softens into gravy. 5. Serve hot with 2 freshly roasted bajra rotis.
benefits: Fenugreek seeds contain galactomannan which slows glucose and lipid absorption in the gut, ideal for diabetic management.
tips: Boiling methi seeds and discarding water completely removes the bitter bite while retaining active phytochemicals.

name: Jain Moong Dal Chilla (2 Chillas) with Mint Chutney & Curd
ingredients: Mint leaves & green chili chutney - 1 tbsp
recipe: 1. Blend soaked yellow moong dal with green chili, cumin, hing, and salt into a pourable batter (strictly zero onion, garlic, or ginger). 2. Heat a non-stick tawa, spread ladle of batter into a thin round crepe. 3. Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil, cook until golden and flip. 4. Serve 2 hot protein chillas with 100g fresh curd and homemade mint chutney.
benefits: High protein density (18g) from pure moong dal with low glycemic index and gentle digestion, fully Jain compliant.
tips: Hing and cumin give the chilla a savory kick without needing any alliums.

name: Jain Paneer Tikka (Oven / Tawa Roasted) with Capsicum & Curd Dip
ingredients: Kasuri methi, ajwain & roasted besan - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Whisk hung curd with mustard oil, roasted besan, ajwain, kasuri methi, and chaat masala (strictly no ginger, garlic, or onion). 2. Coat paneer cubes and capsicum chunks thoroughly in marinade. Rest 10 minutes. 3. Roast on a hot greased grill pan or oven at 200°C for 12 minutes until charred at edges. 4. Squeeze lemon juice and enjoy.
benefits: 26g bioavailable protein with minimal carbohydrates, satisfying the post-workout anabolic leucine requirement.
tips: Ajwain and roasted besan in the marinade give signature tandoori crust without commercial pastes.

name: Jain Soya Chunks Tomato Curry with 2 Whole Wheat Phulkas
recipe: 1. Boil soya chunks in salted water for 5 minutes, squeeze thoroughly. 2. Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and hing. 3. Add fresh tomato puree, green chili, and ground spices (strictly zero onion or garlic). Cook until oil glazes the sides. 4. Add soya chunks and 1/2 cup water; simmer 6 minutes. 5. Serve with 2 soft wheat phulkas.
benefits: 30g complete vegetable protein at less than ₹25 cost, zero alliums, and high satiety.
tips: Pureeing ripe red tomatoes provides natural body and richness to Jain curries.

name: Quick Hard-Boiled Egg Salad with Black Pepper & Lemon (3 Whites + 1 Whole)
ingredients: Pre-boiled eggs - 3 egg whites + 1 whole egg
recipe: 1. Slice pre-boiled egg whites and 1 whole egg into bite-sized rounds. 2. Place in a bowl with diced crunchy cucumber. 3. Season with freshly ground black pepper, chaat masala, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. 4. Enjoy immediately with zero cleanup.
benefits: Instant post-workout recovery: 21g pure albumin protein with high leucine bioavailability and near-zero carbohydrate load.
tips: Boil half a dozen eggs on Sunday night to have pre-boiled protein ready for under-2-minute snacks all week.

name: High-Protein Curd & Soya Chunks Chaat (Pre-Soaked Ready Bowl)
ingredients: Pre-boiled & chilled soya granules - 40g raw equivalent
recipe: 1. Take chilled pre-boiled soya granules. 2. Mix with fresh creamy curd and diced cucumber. 3. Season with roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and black salt. 4. Garnish with torn fresh mint leaves and enjoy.
benefits: Dual protein blend of slow-digesting milk casein and rapid plant soya, delivering 26g protein with zero stove cooking.
tips: Keep boiled soya granules in a Tupperware in your fridge for instant protein salads.

name: Kolkata Chicken Chaap (Low-Oil Fitness Version) with 2 Phulkas
ingredients: Saffron, mace & kewra water - a pinch
recipe: 1. Marinate chicken with hung curd, posto-cashew paste, ginger-garlic, mace, and nutmeg powder. 2. Sear chicken in 1 tsp ghee on wide flat pan. 3. Add marinade, cover, and slow-cook on low flame for 18 minutes until tender and glossy. 4. Serve with 2 freshly made whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: High biological value protein with aromatic spices that aid digestion without excess heavy restaurant oils.
tips: Slow-cooking covered traps moisture so lean chicken remains succulent.

name: Bengali Lau Chingri (Bottle Gourd with Prawns) & Steamed Rice
recipe: 1. Sauté prawns lightly with turmeric for 1.5 minutes; set aside. 2. In same mustard oil, temper cumin seeds and bay leaf. 3. Add shredded bottle gourd, turmeric, and slit chilies. Cook covered without adding water—the gourd releases its own natural juices. 4. Add sautéed prawns, simmer 4 minutes until juices reduce. 5. Serve with 1 cup steamed rice.
benefits: Prawns provide ultra-lean, high-leucine protein and zinc, while bottle gourd provides hydrating soluble fiber and electrolytes.
tips: Do not overcook prawns to keep them soft and tender.
servingUnit: 1 Bowl Lau Chingri + 1 Cup Steamed Rice

name: Bengali Masoor Dal with Jeera & 2 Phulkas
recipe: 1. Boil masoor dal with turmeric, green chili, and salt until completely soft and whisked. 2. Heat mustard oil, add nigella seeds and sliced onions; fry until deep golden. 3. Pour into dal and let it bubble for 2 minutes. 4. Serve with 2 soft whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: Masoor dal cooks in under 15 minutes, provides rich dietary iron, and has high digestibility.
tips: Tempering with mustard oil and nigella seeds is the hallmark of Bengali home-cooked dal.

name: Bengali Posto Bora (Crispy Poppy Seed Patties - 3 pieces) with Rice & Dal
ingredients: Poppy seeds (khus khus / posto) - 35g ground thick
Green chili & onion - 1 tbsp finely chopped
Mustard oil - 1 tsp for shallow pan sear
recipe: 1. Grind poppy seeds with green chili and salt into a thick paste with minimal water. 2. Mix with chopped onion. 3. Form into 3 flat patties. 4. Shallow sear on tawa in 1 tsp mustard oil until crusty and golden. 5. Serve alongside steamed rice and yellow moong dal.
benefits: Poppy seeds are rich in magnesium, calcium, and sleep-regulating compounds that calm the central nervous system after workouts.
tips: Use ice-cold water while grinding posto to keep the paste thick and easy to shape.

name: Gujarati Ringna No Oro (Charred Smoked Eggplant) with 2 Bajra Rotis
ingredients: Large round bharta brinjal (eggplant) - 1 charred and mashed
recipe: 1. Roast eggplant over open flame until skin is completely blistered and flesh is smoky soft. Peel and mash. 2. Heat oil, sauté garlic, spring onions, and green chili. 3. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft. 4. Stir in smoky eggplant mash, season with salt and turmeric. 5. Serve with 2 hot roasted bajra rotis.
benefits: Smoky eggplant delivers nasunin (anthocyanin antioxidant) which protects brain cell lipids from oxidative damage.
tips: Roast a whole garlic clove inside the eggplant slit for deep rustic Gujarati oro flavor.
servingUnit: 1 Bowl Ringna No Oro + 2 Bajra Rotis

name: Gujarati Fajeto (Spiced Mango & Buttermilk Kadhi) with Steamed Rice
ingredients: Mustard seeds, cumin, cloves & cinnamon - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Whisk buttermilk with fresh mango pulp, besan, ginger, turmeric, and salt. 2. Simmer on low heat for 8 minutes while stirring. 3. In a tadka pan, heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, and curry leaves. 4. Pour tadka into bubbling fajeto. 5. Serve alongside 1 cup steamed rice.
benefits: Traditional probiotic summer cooler: combines sweet mango enzymes with gut-friendly lactic acid and spices to improve nutrient assimilation.
tips: Whisk continuously until the first boil to prevent buttermilk curdling.
servingUnit: 1 Deep Bowl Fajeto + 1 Cup Steamed Rice

name: Gujarati Vaghareli Khichdi with Dahi & Garlic Chutney
ingredients: Toor dal or split green moong - 40g
Mustard seeds, cumin, cloves & hing - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Heat 1 tsp ghee in pressure cooker, add mustard seeds, cumin, cloves, and hing. 2. Add diced vegetables, dal, rice, turmeric, chili, and 3.5 cups water. 3. Pressure cook for 4 whistles until porridge-soft. 4. Serve with 100g fresh curd and spicy garlic chutney.
benefits: Balanced vegetable-lentil-grain thali in a single pot, warming, comforting, and restorative for training recovery.
tips: Adding cloves and hing in the vaghar provides natural digestive carminative properties.

name: Gujarati Sprouted Kala Chana Kathol with 2 Phulkas
recipe: 1. Pressure cook sprouted kala chana with salt and water for 4 whistles. 2. Heat oil, add ajwain and hing. 3. Add boiled chana with its mineral broth, cumin-coriander powder, turmeric, and amchur. 4. Simmer 6 minutes until gravy is thick. 5. Serve with 2 whole wheat phulkas.
benefits: Rich in dietary iron, plant protein, and slowly fermented prebiotic fiber that prevents blood sugar spikes.
tips: Sprouting desi chana shortens cooking time and unlocks mineral bioavailability.

name: Rajasthani Ker Sangri with 2 Bajra Rotis & Curd
ingredients: Amchur, red chili & coriander powder - 1 tsp
recipe: 1. Soak ker and sangri overnight, boil in salted water for 8 minutes and drain. 2. Heat mustard oil, add cumin and hing. 3. Add boiled ker sangri, amchur, red chili, and coriander powder; sauté on medium heat for 6 minutes. 4. Serve with 2 freshly made hot bajra rotis and 100g curd.
benefits: Desert superfoods ker and sangri are naturally loaded with saponins, flavonoids, and dietary fiber adapted for arid resilience.
tips: Washing ker-sangri 3 times after soaking removes any desert sand and excess tartness.
servingUnit: 1 Bowl Ker Sangri + 2 Bajra Rotis + Curd

name: Rajasthani Moong Dal Mangodi ki Sabzi with 2 Phulkas
recipe: 1. Lightly crush mangodi and roast in 1/2 tsp oil until golden and aromatic. 2. In same pan, add remaining oil, cumin, hing, and tomato puree with dry spices. 3. Add 1.5 cups water and bring to boil. 4. Add roasted mangodi, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until mangodi is soft and juicy. 5. Serve with 2 warm phulkas.
benefits: Traditional sun-dried moong mangodi concentrates pulse protein and enzymes, providing long shelf life and quick home cooking.
tips: Lightly roasting mangodi before boiling keeps them firm and prevents them from breaking into mush.

name: Rajasthani Bajra Khichdi with Fresh Curd & Garlic Chutney
recipe: 1. Soak cracked bajra for 2 hours. 2. In pressure cooker, heat ghee, crackle cumin seeds and hing. 3. Add soaked bajra, moong dal, turmeric, salt, and 4 cups water. 4. Pressure cook on medium-low for 5 whistles until thick and porridge-like. 5. Serve warm with 100g fresh curd.
benefits: Pearl millet (bajra) is high in slowly digestible starch and iron, delivering sustained energy release without post-meal fatigue.
tips: Soaking cracked bajra thoroughly ensures a silky, non-gritty khichdi texture.

name: Jain Handvo (Baked Bottle Gourd & Lentil Cake) with Mint Chutney
ingredients: Fermented mixed pulse batter (chana, toor, moong, rice) - 70g
recipe: 1. Mix fermented lentil batter with grated lauki, green chili, turmeric, and salt (zero onion, garlic, or ginger). 2. Add eno, pour into a pan tempered with mustard and sesame seeds. 3. Cook covered on low heat for 10 minutes until bottom crust is golden, flip and crisp top. 4. Slice and serve with Jain mint chutney.
benefits: High dietary fiber and complete plant proteins from 3 pulses and rice, fully compliant with strict Jain dietary rules.
tips: Use bottle gourd (lauki) for moisture instead of any root vegetable.

name: Jain Gujarati Kadhi with Steamed Basmati Rice
recipe: 1. Whisk curd with besan, 1.5 cups water, and salt until completely smooth. 2. Simmer on low heat while stirring. 3. Temper with ghee, cumin seeds, mustard seeds, cloves, cinnamon, hing, and slit green chili (zero ginger, garlic, or onion). 4. Pour crackling tadka into kadhi. 5. Serve with 1 cup steamed basmati rice.
benefits: Probiotic-rich comforting meal that soothes the stomach lining and promotes efficient protein digestion.
tips: Stirring continuously until the first boil prevents the curd from curdling.
servingUnit: 1 Bowl Jain Kadhi + 1 Cup Steamed Rice
